# Leggett & Platt (LEG) — Forensic Dossier
*Interrogator — Claude Opus 4.8 · transcripts FY2024 Q1 → FY2025 Q4 (bundled) · financials per screener + live FMP*

> **Framing note (load-bearing):** Every word in these transcripts predates the event that now governs the stock. On **December 1, 2025** Somnigroup International (SGI) made a public unsolicited proposal to buy LEG for ~$12.00/share, and on **April 13, 2026** the two boards signed a **definitive all-stock merger** at a fixed **0.1455 SGI per LEG**. LEG **withdrew 2026 guidance** and **cancelled its earnings call** with the Q1-2026 print (May 7, 2026). So the transcripts below are the *standalone-turnaround* story — useful only as evidence of what kind of asset SGI is buying and why a strategic acquirer (LEG's largest customer) found it cheap enough to take out. Read the credibility of the turnaround narrative through that lens, not as a live investable thesis.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The arc across these eight quarters is a textbook **"defend the balance sheet, shrink to greatness, wait for the cycle"** story — and, critically, it *delivered on the controllables while the topline kept eroding*.

- **Q1-2024 (the capitulation):** New-then CEO Mitch Dolloff opens by *re-explaining who the company even is* ("who we are, where we stand today and where we are going") — a tell that the narrative had lost the market. Three priorities are set that never change for two years: **(1) strengthen the balance sheet/liquidity, (2) improve margins via restructuring + G&A, (3) position for profitable growth.** The dividend is **cut to $0.05** ("following a very thorough evaluation") and the revolver leverage covenant is loosened **3.5x → 4.0x** through mid-2025 — a defensive liquidity grab. A January-2024 restructuring plan (footprint consolidation) is already underway.
- **Q2-2024 (leadership reset):** Karl Glassman *returns as CEO* in late May ("hit the ground running"), bringing a sharper, more operational tone. He introduces the language that defines the rest of the arc: **portfolio review** ("are we the rightful owner of each business?") and the promise of a **comprehensive long-term vision with financial targets mid-2025.** Buybacks flagged as a *future* capital-return tool once debt is down.
- **Q3-2024 (the portfolio knife comes out):** The strategic review produces its first concrete output — **"exploring the potential sale of our Aerospace business."** Restructuring is "ahead of schedule and exceeding expectations." ~$10M corporate G&A savings identified for 2025. Auto headwinds reframed from cyclical to **structural** (Chinese EV share loss).
- **Q3-2025 (the deleveraging victory lap):** **Aerospace divested Aug 29, 2025**; proceeds + cash retire **all commercial paper**; net-debt/EBITDA cut to **2.6x** (~2.9x pro-forma ex-Aero) vs the 4.0x covenant ceiling. Debt down **$296M in the quarter, $367M YTD.** Restructuring "nearing completion," EBIT benefit **$60–70M annualized**, real-estate proceeds **$70–80M.** Tone shifts from survival to *"positioned to accelerate when residential turns."*
- **Q4-2025 (the finished product):** Restructuring "substantially complete… greater EBIT benefit at lower cost than originally expected." Long-term leverage target of **2x** in sight. Full-year OCF **$338M** (+$33M YoY) on *falling* sales — the cash-conversion proof point. Residential end-markets (≈half of revenue) described as **"a multiyear depression."** Guidance for 2026: bedding down LSD, specialized roughly flat ex-Aero. The story is now: *we have built a leaner, deleveraged, cash-generative company and we are waiting for volume.*

**Drivers introduced and kept:** semi-finished/ComfortCore content gains, Geo Components (civil construction + retail share gains at home-improvement big-box), Textiles (medical nonwovens, engineered materials), metal-margin/trade-rod. **Drivers quietly dropped or reframed:** the once-core dividend (gone as a thesis pillar); Automotive growth (downgraded to "perform in line with market, -1% to -2%"); Specialty Foam and Adjustable Bed (recast from businesses to *fix-and-shrink* problems anchored to two lost customers, incl. Mattress Firm).

**The arc the transcripts could not see coming:** none of this prepared shareholders for a *takeover*. The narrative was "self-help into an eventual cyclical recovery." Instead, **SGI — the world's largest bedding company and a key LEG customer — concluded the deleveraged-but-cheap asset was worth vertically integrating**, and the standalone story was overtaken by an all-stock bid.

The story across these five quarters is remarkably consistent and, crucially, **defensive throughout** — a self-help turnaround inside a multi-year residential demand depression, not a growth story.

**Drivers quietly dropped:** aerospace (sold), and any pretense of top-line growth — every call walks revenue *down*.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across these five quarters management told one remarkably consistent story: *"the end markets are in a multi-year depression we cannot control, so we are pulling every internal lever — restructuring, cost, debt paydown, portfolio pruning — to be ready when the cycle finally turns."* The opening call (fourth quarter of 2024) framed 2024 as "a year of significant change" built around a restructuring plan that beat its own targets ("$22 million of EBIT benefit… exceeded our expectation of $10 million to $15 million"). By the middle of 2025 the plan was "largely complete"; by the fourth quarter of 2025 it was "substantially completed… greater EBIT benefit at lower cost than originally expected."

First, **portfolio simplification** became concrete: the exploration of an aerospace sale (early 2025) turned into a signed agreement (first quarter of 2025), then a completed divestiture for about $240 million after-tax (closed August 29, 2025), the proceeds of which retired all commercial paper. The thread that was *quietly dropped* is any near-term growth story. Each call pushed the recovery further out ("we cannot predict the timing of demand recovery") until, in the final call, residential end markets were described flatly as being "in a multi-year depression with demand well below average cycle levels." The narrative arc is therefore a managed decline: shrink the base, fix the cost structure, protect the balance sheet, and wait.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The hard numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Restructuring delivered greater EBIT benefit at lower cost than expected" (Q4-25) | Adjusted EBIT still *fell* $4M in 2025 to $263M; adjusted EPS flat at $1.05. **Trajectory: Stable, and defensive throughout.** This is not a management team that oscillated; it is one that settled into a defensive crouch early and held it. The language is overwhelmingly about *control the controllable*: "prioritize balance sheet strength, operational efficiency, and margin improvement" recurs almost verbatim across all five calls. Offensive, growth-oriented language is rare and always hedged ("position the company to accelerate *when* residential end markets turn").

**Reliability: Medium-to-High on what they control, and refreshingly un-sandbagged on what they don't.** Restructuring guidance was serially *beaten* — the EBIT benefit exceeded the initial range, sales attrition came in far below the initial $40M fear (only ~$15M in 2024), and real-estate proceeds ran ahead of plan. The aerospace divestiture was guided, signed, and closed on schedule for the promised ~$240M. That is a credible operating team.

Against that, the *demand* guidance was repeatedly cut — bedding volume expectations were lowered through 2025, and the fourth-quarter-2025 call guided bedding down again for 2026. But management flagged these cuts early and attributed them to nameable causes (two specific customers — Mattress Firm consolidation and a private-label program taken in-house — plus merchandising changes), rather than hiding them. Analysts (Piper Sandler's Keith, Goldman's Maklari, Truist's Hughes) circled the same three worries every quarter. **First, when does the mattress cycle turn** — management never gave a date, and each quarter proved the caution warranted. **Second, import/transshipment enforcement** — management grew *more* specific and more optimistic here over time (the fourth-quarter-2025 detail on a dismantled "$400 million" transshipment scheme and 75% of tested imports failing flammability rules), a rare area where they leaned in. **Third, margin durability in Furniture, Flooring & Textiles** — this is where they were most exposed: pressed on the sharp fourth-quarter-2025 FF&T margin drop, Sam Smith conceded pricing pressure in flooring and textiles plus greenfield Vietnam start-up costs, i.e. the softest part of the story. 🔴 **The dividend was gutted** — now a token $0.05/quarter (declared for the second quarter of 2026), a shadow of the former "Dividend King." Zero open-market insider buying.
🔴 **FF&T margin cliff** in the fourth quarter of 2025, partly structural (flooring demand, competitive discounting).
🟢 **Balance sheet genuinely repaired** — $367M debt cut in 2025, commercial paper zeroed, leverage down to 2.6x.
🟢 **Restructuring over-delivered** and the benefits are described as sustainable.
🟢 **Content gains are real** — semi-finished bedding (ComfortCore, EcoBase) grew 20%+ and lifts price per unit even when volumes are flat.
🟢 **Portfolio pruning executed cleanly** (aerospace sold at a fair price, small non-core units divested).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The IR chair rotated three times in a year (Branscum → West → Kleiboeker), unusual churn but with no thesis content. More telling is the *rebranding of the automotive segment to "Leggett Dynamics"* in June 2026 with a technology/"software-defined motion" identity — a late attempt to reframe a declining, ICE-exposed auto-components business as a growth story, which reads as narrative management more than a fundamental shift. The subtlest tell across the calls is the migration of the growth language from *volume* to *content and mix* ("all of those end up being multiples in terms of the selling price"): a tacit admission that unit growth is not coming back, so the only path to profit growth is selling more per unit into a flat-to-shrinking market. That is a mature-to-declining business talking.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STABLE — a competently-run, self-repairing melt.** Management did exactly what a good team does with a structurally challenged, over-levered asset: cut cost, sold non-core pieces, paid down debt, and protected optionality on the eventual cycle turn. They earned their credibility. But the single most important thing the director must weigh is that **none of that matters to the return anymore.** As of April 2026 this is not a standalone investment; it is a fixed-ratio, all-stock claim on Somnigroup. The standalone franchise the acquirer is buying has an **eroding moat** — a real scale position in U.S. innersprings (a leading domestic manufacturer, a cost-and-footprint advantage) but with *falling* returns (ROIC ~8% and drifting down), a thin and only-stable gross margin, and a five-year revenue slide. The threat is more cyclical-plus-share-loss (imported/transshipped mattresses, ICE-to-EV auto mix) than a clean terminal-technology wipeout, so it reads **material, not terminal** — but the direction of travel is unmistakably down. The cheapness on standalone metrics is a value-trap risk, which is precisely why the board sold.

The IR chair rotated three times in a year (Branscum → West → Kleiboeker), unusual churn but with no thesis content. ## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STABLE — a competently-run, self-repairing melt.** Management did exactly what a good team does with a structurally challenged, over-levered asset: cut cost, sold non-core pieces, paid down debt, and protected optionality on the eventual cycle turn.
